articles.title: AI policy
articles.requirement: The organisation shall establish an AI policy that is appropriate to its purpose, provides a framework for setting objectives, includes commitment to compliance, and is communicated and available.

articles.title: Internal organisation roles and responsibilities for AI
articles.requirement: The organisation shall define and allocate responsibilities and authorities for AI system governance, development, deployment, and monitoring, ensuring accountability at all levels.

articles.title: Resources for AI
articles.requirement: The organisation shall determine and provide resources needed for the establishment, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of the AIMS, including human, technological, and financial resources.

articles.title: Assessing AI risks
articles.requirement: The organisation shall assess risks associated with AI systems, considering potential negative impacts on individuals, groups, and society, and the likelihood and severity of harm.

articles.title: AI risk treatment
articles.requirement: The organisation shall determine and implement AI risk treatment options, selecting controls to address identified risks and documenting the rationale for treatment decisions.

articles.title: AI system impact assessment
articles.requirement: The organisation shall conduct impact assessments for AI systems, evaluating potential consequences for affected stakeholders, human rights, safety, fairness, and societal well-being.

articles.title: Documentation of AI system impact assessment
articles.requirement: The organisation shall document the results of AI system impact assessments including scope, methodology, identified impacts, mitigation measures, and residual risks.

articles.title: Responsible AI — objectives and values
articles.requirement: The organisation shall define responsible AI values and objectives covering fairness, transparency, explainability, accountability, robustness, safety, and privacy as applicable.

articles.title: Intended use and context of AI systems
articles.requirement: The organisation shall determine and document the intended use and operational context of each AI system, including intended users, operating environment, and foreseeable misuse.

articles.title: AI system design and development
articles.requirement: The organisation shall apply processes for the design and development of AI systems, including requirements specification, architecture, model selection, training, testing, and validation.

articles.title: Verification and validation of AI systems
articles.requirement: The organisation shall verify and validate AI systems to ensure they meet specified requirements, including performance, fairness, robustness, and security criteria.

articles.title: AI system lifecycle management
articles.requirement: The organisation shall manage AI systems throughout their lifecycle, from planning and design through deployment, operation, monitoring, and eventual retirement or decommissioning.

articles.title: AI data quality
articles.requirement: The organisation shall ensure the quality of data used in AI systems including accuracy, completeness, timeliness, relevance, and representativeness, and address data biases.

articles.title: AI data provenance and lineage
articles.requirement: The organisation shall record and maintain the provenance and lineage of data used in AI systems, including sources, transformations, and processing history.

articles.title: Data for AI — acquisition and preparation
articles.requirement: The organisation shall establish processes for data acquisition, labelling, annotation, and preparation, ensuring consistency, quality, and appropriateness for the intended AI application.

articles.title: AI system transparency
articles.requirement: The organisation shall provide transparency about its AI systems proportionate to the context, enabling stakeholders to understand AI involvement, capabilities, limitations, and decision logic.

articles.title: AI system explainability
articles.requirement: The organisation shall provide explanations of AI system outputs and decisions at a level appropriate to the context, audience, and potential impact on affected parties.

articles.title: Engagement of interested parties
articles.requirement: The organisation shall identify and engage with interested parties affected by AI systems, considering their needs, expectations, and concerns throughout the AI system lifecycle.

articles.title: Reporting of AI system behaviour
articles.requirement: The organisation shall establish mechanisms for reporting AI system behaviour, including anomalous outputs, unexpected impacts, and incidents, with escalation procedures.

articles.title: Recording of AI system events
articles.requirement: The organisation shall establish logging and recording mechanisms for AI system events including inputs, outputs, decisions, performance metrics, and changes to the system.

articles.title: Monitoring of AI systems
articles.requirement: The organisation shall monitor AI systems in operation for performance, accuracy, fairness, robustness, and alignment with intended use, taking corrective action when needed.

articles.title: AI system performance evaluation
articles.requirement: The organisation shall evaluate AI system performance against defined metrics and criteria, review results at planned intervals, and use findings to drive improvement.

articles.title: Third-party AI providers and components
articles.requirement: The organisation shall assess risks associated with third-party AI components, services, and models, establishing requirements and controls for procurement, integration, and ongoing use.

articles.title: Provision of AI systems to third parties
articles.requirement: The organisation shall provide adequate information to third parties receiving its AI systems, including intended use, limitations, known risks, and guidance for responsible deployment.

articles.title: Competence and awareness for AI
articles.requirement: The organisation shall determine necessary competence for persons doing work affecting AI system performance, ensure they are competent through education, training, or experience, and raise awareness.

articles.title: Human oversight of AI systems
articles.requirement: The organisation shall implement human oversight mechanisms proportionate to the risk and impact of AI systems, enabling humans to understand, intervene, and override AI outputs.

articles.title: AI system continual improvement
articles.requirement: The organisation shall continually improve the suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the AIMS, using monitoring results, audits, incident findings, and stakeholder feedback.

articles.title: Documentation and record management for AI
articles.requirement: The organisation shall maintain documented information required by the AIMS, including policies, procedures, risk assessments, impact assessments, and system records.

articles.title: Compliance with legal and regulatory requirements for AI
articles.requirement: The organisation shall identify and comply with applicable legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements related to AI systems, including data protection, safety, and sector-specific legislation.

articles.title: Internal audit of the AIMS
articles.requirement: The organisation shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to determine whether the AIMS conforms to its own requirements and those of ISO 42001, and is effectively implemented.
